name: Content on Hover or Focus
explanation: This criterion applies whenever hovering a pointer over something, or moving keyboard focus to it, makes extra content appear that wasn't already visible — a tooltip, a dropdown preview, a "more info" popup. If a component does this, it must meet three conditions. Dismissible: the user can make the content go away, typically by pressing Escape, without having to move the pointer elsewhere — unless the content is required to finish the task, or the behavior is a well-established convention like a native browser tooltip. Hoverable: if hover triggered the content, the user must be able to move the pointer onto the new content itself without it disappearing, so they can read or copy text from it. Persistent: the content has to stay visible until the user moves away or dismisses it — it can't vanish on its own after a fixed timeout while they're still trying to read it. The goal is simple: don't show people something and then snatch it away before they can act on it.
whoItAffects: Sighted keyboard-only users rely on focus-triggered tooltips being dismissible without a mouse. If the only way to close a tooltip is to click elsewhere, someone tabbing through a form has no way to get rid of it and continue navigating predictably. People with low vision who use screen magnification often need to move their pointer across the screen to read a zoomed-in region, so a tooltip that disappears the instant the pointer moves toward it makes the content practically unreadable. People with motor impairments or hand tremors may take longer to move the pointer, so content that vanishes on the slightest movement, or auto-dismisses after a short timeout, can disappear before they've read it. Users with cognitive or reading disabilities may simply need more time to process a tooltip's content, which a timed auto-dismiss doesn't allow for.

codeExample.bad: Must be at least 12 characters and include a number.

howToTest: Find a control on the page that reveals extra content on hover or keyboard focus, and check all three behaviors by hand. First, trigger it with the mouse and slowly move the pointer toward the new content. If it disappears before you reach it, that fails Hoverable. Second, trigger it with the keyboard and press Escape without moving focus. If the content doesn't close, that fails Dismissible. Third, trigger it and just wait without moving your mouse. If it disappears on its own after a few seconds while you're still looking at it, that fails Persistent.

check.question: A tooltip appears when a user hovers over an info icon. Moving the mouse even slightly toward the tooltip to read more of it causes the tooltip to immediately disappear. Which part of SC 1.4.13 does this fail?
choices: Dismissible, because the user can't close the tooltip with Escape
Hoverable, because the pointer can't be moved onto the tooltip content without it disappearing
Persistent, because the tooltip closes after a fixed time delay
It doesn't fail 1.4.13 since the tooltip did appear on hover
